description: The desktop AI apps that make up the bulk of the demo table.
why: The four bundle ids that used to be must_contain are now must_find on the classifier, which is the layer that actually knows them. com.openai.codex is ChatGPT Desktop, not Codex CLI -- the obvious guess, com.openai.chat, is wrong, and pinning it here is the only thing that would catch a catalog edit getting it backwards. lm-studio and jan are Local model entries rather than agents, and are here because this is the scenario that installs casks -- the classification describes deployment shape, and their shape is a desktop app.
known_gaps: Windsurf's Homebrew token is `devin-desktop`, not `windsurf`. Read off the Homebrew API; a scenario written from the product name would install nothing and the WARN would scroll past.

Installing a cask proves the bundle id is right. It does not launch the app, so no scenario here observes a launchd job, a listening port or a state directory that only appears on first GUI launch -- `open -a` needs an Aqua session and there is none over SSH.
These are paid or account-gated products in several cases. The install is unattended and the SIGN-IN is not, so nothing here exercises behaviour that only appears once a user is authenticated.
